title: BRIDGE for Workers Act
official_summary:
Building on Reemployment Improvements to Deliver Good Employment for Workers Act or the BRIDGE for Workers Act

This act permanently expands the allowable purposes for certain Department of Labor grants to states for reemployment services and eligibility assessments. Specifically, the act permanently allows these grants to be used to fund reemployment services and eligibility assessments for all claimants for unemployment compensation.

(Under the current statute, the grants may only be used to provide such services to a subset of claimants who have been identified by the state as likely to exhaust unemployment benefits and need job search assistance to become employed. However, in recent years, annual appropriations acts have allowed the grants to be used for all claimants for unemployment compensation. This act makes this authority permanent.)

summary.headline: Law permanently lets states use federal job-help grants to serve everyone who files for unemployment benefits, not just a smaller group.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes rules for Department of Labor grants that pay states to offer reemployment services and eligibility checks to people claiming unemployment benefits. Before, the law said these grants could only serve claimants the state flagged as likely to run out of benefits and needing job search help. Yearly spending bills had been allowing the grants to cover all claimants. This law makes that broader use permanent.

who_it_affects.group: People who file for unemployment benefits
who_it_affects.how: Any claimant, not just those flagged as likely to run out of benefits, can be served by these grant-funded job search services and eligibility reviews.
States can permanently use these federal grants for all unemployment claimants without relying on yearly spending bill language.
The department's grants to states for reemployment services now permanently cover all unemployment claimants.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted November 25, 2024; the summary does not state a separate start date.
